clue.text: Firm with little money and evidence of debt in profusion

definitions.note: a phrase standing for an adjective meaning plentiful

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
P, a penny, is a small sum of money
IOUs are written promises to repay, so evidence of debt

explanation.surface: A struggling company, short of cash, is buried under a pile of unpaid notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something present in profusion is plentiful or abundant.

clue.text: King using corporal punishment to contain rising workers

indicators.note: the punishment word is said to hold the workers inside it

parts.note: the cane was used for corporal punishment in schools

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the workers' letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: TU, a trade union, is a body of workers

explanation.surface: A monarch threatens beatings to keep rebellious labourers in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the union's letters upwards, and 'to contain' wraps the punishment around them; 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute was an eleventh-century king of England, Denmark and Norway, famed for the tale of commanding the tide.

clue.text: Old equipment mounted in secure framework to produce crude metal

indicators.note: the old equipment is placed inside the word for secure

parts.note: to pin something is to fasten it securely

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: Antique machinery is fixed into a sturdy frame to make rough iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns ORIG into GIRO, which goes inside PIN; 'framework' merely dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is the impure iron first tapped from a blast furnace, before refining.

clue.text: In line of succession to throne when restored? Exactly!

indicators.note: restored suggests putting the letters back into a new order

parts.note: T, as in the phrase 'to a T', meaning exactly

explanation.surface: A claimant asks whether the next heir would be back on the throne, and is told yes, precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when restored' rearranges TO THRONE; T comes from 'to a T', meaning exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: On the trot means one after another, consecutively, as in a line of successors.

clue.text: Marvellous kind of patient with nurse in support to oversee operations

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece in support sits underneath, so it comes last

parts.note: super is informal for marvellous
an in-patient stays in hospital, so IN is a kind of patient
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A hospital ward where a splendid in-patient and a nurse help run the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in support' puts TEND at the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To superintend is to direct and supervise work being done.

clue.text: Dispose of litter, including second tiny dog

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Clearing away rubbish, including the mess left by a very small puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep up is to clear away rubbish with a brush.

clue.text: Be on the bench, following second appeal

indicators.note: the appeal comes after the second, following it in the answer

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A judge takes the bench after a second appeal is lodged.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges sit in court, so to be on the bench is to hold session as a judge.

clue.text: Fragrant resin, note, in tree I found

indicators.note: the note is placed inside the tree

parts.note: the elm is a tree
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a sweet-smelling gum while hunting through the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside ELM, then I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic gum resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Precious stone acquired by means of one dowry

parts.note: per means through or by means of
I is the Roman numeral one
dot is a dowry, from French

explanation.surface: A bride's family hands over a jewel as part of her marriage settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: DOT is an old word for a dowry, borrowed from French.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a form of olivine.

clue.text: Openings admitting beam for projection of pictures

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for a verb meaning depicts; the definition is loose

indicators.note: the openings let the beam in, so it goes inside them

parts.note: ports are openings, as in a ship's portholes
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Light streams through apertures to throw images on a screen, as in a cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict or represent in pictures or words.

clue.text: Late entertainment centre near Main Street rejected

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: top, as in chief or main

explanation.surface: A club open after hours by the high street is turned down by the planners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns TOPST into TSPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightspot is a nightclub, a venue for entertainment late in the evening.

clue.text: Slip's dismay, dropping opener

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: losing its opening letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: terror is extreme fear or dismay

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified at a slip they have made while losing a cricket opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping opener' removes the T from TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a minor mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Tip of the tongue, in short

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here of 'the'

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language, a tongue

explanation.surface: Something hovering on the tip of the tongue, said briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tongue' here is a language, Erse (Irish or Scottish Gaelic), not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse means brief and curt, using few words.

clue.text: One who jogs without a rest

indicators.note: without means outside, so the jogger word surrounds the a

parts.note: a reminder is something that jogs the memory

explanation.surface: A runner keeps going without stopping for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jogs' is about memory, not running; 'without' is the old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over, the rest.

clue.text: Tension developed when housed in friend's dwelling

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are lodged inside the friend's word

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters have changed shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strain grows when someone moves into a pal's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' shuffles the clue's first word, and 'when housed in' lodges the result inside the friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A maisonette is a self-contained flat on two floors, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Travelling mostly without hardship, showing tenacity

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: in transit means travelling
gently means mildly, without harshness

explanation.surface: Journeying with little discomfort shows great persistence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last T of IN TRANSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigently means stubbornly, refusing to compromise, so with tenacity.

clue.text: Next crisis almost breaking? It's coming from outside

indicators.note: breaking means broken up, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the last letter of crisis is dropped

explanation.surface: The next emergency is about to erupt, and it is external.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CRISIS to CRISI; 'breaking' rearranges NEXT CRISI.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrinsic means external, originating outside the thing concerned.

clue.text: Become more unobservant and innocent

definitions.meaning: to ... is to notice fewer things
pure, without a stain on one's character

explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means clean and so morally blameless, while split it means notice fewer things.

clue.text: Celebrate lavishly to get cruise under way?

definitions.meaning: to spend freely on a celebration
literally, launch a vessel to set out on a voyage

explanation.surface: Someone throws a lavish party to launch a holiday cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spend extravagantly, and literally describes launching a ship.

clue.text: Like an author, quiet as a bird

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
avian means of or like birds

explanation.surface: A writer is described as being as silent as a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The author is George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shavian means relating to or in the manner of George Bernard Shaw, the playwright.

clue.text: Cocky newcomer riding over jump

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so this comes first

parts.note: up means riding, as a jockey is up on a horse
a start is a sudden jump of surprise

explanation.surface: A brash new jockey clears a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone who has risen suddenly and acts arrogantly.

clue.text: Go straight and become sociable

explanation.definitionFit: To unbend is both to straighten and to relax one's stiff manner.

clue.text: Awful display of greed at an outdoor restaurant

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Diners guzzling at an open-air cafe make a terrible show of gluttony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges GREED AT AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an open-air place serving refreshments.

clue.text: Eastern ruler making a simple pronouncement

indicators.note: a pronouncement is spoken, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a mere, as in nothing more than

explanation.surface: An oriental potentate issues a plain decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouncement' signals that 'a mere' is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: An ameer, or emir, is a Muslim prince or governor.

clue.text: Writer using nibs with pen, but not initially

indicators.note: each word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: An author writes with a fountain pen, though not at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops N from NIBS and P from PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House.

clue.text: Pick a particular size of type

definitions.meaning: the best, as in the pick of the bunch
a typewriter type size of twelve characters per inch

explanation.definitionFit: Elite means the best few, and is also a typewriter typeface size.

clue.text: Not willing to declare after batting with only half of team

indicators.note: the declaring word comes after the other pieces

parts.note: in cricket, a side batting is in

indicators.note: only the first half of the word team is used

parts.note: to state is to declare

explanation.surface: A cricket captain declines to declare while batting with only half the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half of' keeps the first two letters of the side; 'after' puts the declaring verb last. Batting side in cricket is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intestate means dying without having made a will.

clue.text: Demon driving up motorway and parking at the end

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with 1 read as I
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: A fiend drives up the motorway and parks at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; 'driving up' turns MI into IM.
explanation.definitionFit: An imp is a small demon or mischievous sprite.

clue.text: Daily gin in a warm nook

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Someone sits with a newspaper and a gin in a cosy corner.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British daily tabloid; a gin is also a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered sunny spot.

clue.text: Left interrupted by Conservative full of passion

indicators.note: the Conservative breaks into the word for left

parts.note: exited means left, went out

explanation.surface: A Tory heckler breaks into a departing speaker's fervent address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' means departed, not the political side.
explanation.definitionFit: Excited means stirred up, full of strong feeling.
